title: kate-search: skip an empty whole-word find
summary: An empty needle with whole words returns no hits. An empty needle without that flag still reports the empty spans. The test goes in the existing literal tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition: fn find(rope: &Rope, needle: &str, case_sensitive: bool, whole_words: bool, start: usize, end: usize) -> Vec<Match>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: literal.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Keep find pub(crate). At the start of find, one if returns early: if needle.is_empty() && whole_words { return Vec::new(); }. Delete the later if that retains empty whole-word spans. Do not nest an if inside an if. Do not touch empty_spans, find_exact, find_folded, is_whole_word, is_word_char, or is_boundary. The existing test an_apostrophe_is_inside_a_word stays green. The test an_empty_whole_word_finds_nothing calls super::find on Rope::from_str of ab. An empty needle, case sensitive, whole words, start 0, end the scalar count, returns an empty vector. The same call with whole words false returns 3 hits. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: literal::tests::an_empty_whole_word_finds_nothing
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. An empty whole-word find on ab returns 2 hits. After the change it returns none. An empty find without whole words still returns 3 hits.
